title: Ethiopian Potato Sambusa
community: All of Ethiopia — the potato-filled street pastry
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Potato Sambusa — the thin crispy sambusa pastry filled with spiced mashed potato, green peas, jalapeño, and coriander. The vegan-friendly sambusa — during fasting periods when lentils are available but meat is not, potato sambusa is the most commonly found.
longDesc: Potato sambusa is the fasting period street vendor's most important offering — the potato filling is filling, inexpensive, and completely vegan. The berbere-spiced potato and pea filling has more body and flavour than it sounds.
ingredients: 3 medium potatoes — boiled and roughly mashed
steps: Make potato filling: mix mashed potato, peas, fried onion, jalapeño, spices, and coriander. Season. Cool.
Shape, fill, and fry as per ETH161 method.
chefTips: The potato must be mashed dry — watery potato breaks the pastry.
Same sealing, same frying technique as ETH161.
commonMistakes: Wet potato filling — same result as wet lentil: broken sambusa.
cookingScience: See ETH161 for sambusa frying science.
sustainabilityTips: Potatoes and peas — entirely plant-based, locally grown.
culturalNote: Potato sambusa is the fasting street food that keeps vendors in business during the 200+ annual Orthodox fasting days — the entirely plant-based sambusa that satisfies the hunger of the fasting Orthodox majority.
